name: Area & Perimeter: 50 Problems
lesson: Perimeter is the distance around the outside boundary. Add boundary sides; shared internal edges are excluded. Lengths use units such as cm or m.
Area measures the surface covered, in square units. For a square, $A=s^{2}$; for a rectangle, $A=lw$.
For a parallelogram, $A=bh$. For a triangle, $A=\frac{1}{2} bh$. The height must be perpendicular to the chosen base, even when it lies outside the figure.
For a trapezoid, $A=\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h$, where $a$ and $b$ are the parallel sides. The perpendicular distance between them is $h$.
To work backward, undo the operations in the area or perimeter formula. For a shaded region, consider subtracting an unshaded piece or adding familiar pieces.

problems.q: A square has side length 8 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: How many square centimetres fit in each row, and how many rows are there?
problems.solution: The square has 8 rows of 8 square centimetres, so its area is $8\times8=64\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A square with one side labelled 8 cm.

problems.q: A square garden has side length 13 m. How much fencing is needed to enclose it?
problems.hint: The fence follows all four sides of the garden.
problems.solution: All four sides are 13 m long. The fencing needed is $4\times13=52\text{ m}$.
problems.imageAlt: A square garden with one side labelled 13 m.

problems.q: A square has perimeter 68 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: First find the length of one of the four equal sides.
problems.solution: Each side is $68\div4=17$ cm. Use that side length for the area: $17\times17=289\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A square labelled perimeter 68 cm. Its side length is unknown.

problems.q: A square has area 196 cm². Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: Which whole number multiplied by itself gives the area?
problems.solution: Since $14\times14=196$, each side is 14 cm. The perimeter is $4\times14=56\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A square labelled area 196 square centimetres. No side lengths are given.

problems.q: Two identical squares, each with side length 7 cm, are joined along one complete side. Find the perimeter of the combined figure.
problems.hint: Trace only the outside boundary. The shared side is inside the figure.
problems.solution: The outside boundary has 6 exposed sides, each 7 cm long. Its perimeter is $6\times7=42\text{ cm}$. Adding the two square perimeters would count the shared side twice.
problems.imageAlt: Two identical squares joined along a full side. A side of one square is labelled 7 cm; the shared edge is dashed.

problems.q: A large square is divided into a 3 × 3 grid of identical squares. Each small square has side length 4 cm. Find the perimeter of the large square.
problems.hint: Find how many small side lengths make one complete outer side.
problems.solution: One outer side contains 3 small sides, so it is $3\times4=12$ cm long. The large square has perimeter $4\times12=48\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A square divided into a 3 by 3 grid. One side of a small cell is labelled 4 cm. The outer side length is unlabelled.

problems.q: A square originally has side length 9 cm. Each side length is increased by 2 cm. By how much does its area increase?
problems.hint: Calculate the area before and after the change, then subtract.
problems.solution: The new side length is $9+2=11$ cm. The increase in area is $11\times11-9\times9=121-81=40\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: Two squares labelled Before and After. The original side is 9 cm. The new side length is unknown; it is 2 cm longer.

problems.q: A square courtyard has side length 15 m. A smaller square of side length 9 m occupies its centre. Find the area of the shaded surrounding region.
problems.hint: Subtract the area of the inner square from the area of the entire courtyard.
problems.solution: The outer area is $15^{2}=225\text{ m}^{2}$ and the inner area is $9^{2}=81\text{ m}^{2}$. The surrounding region has area $225-81=144\text{ m}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A square of side 15 m surrounds a centred square of side 9 m. The region outside the inner square is shaded.

problems.q: A square and an 18 cm by 8 cm rectangle have equal areas. Find the perimeter of the square.
problems.hint: Find the rectangle’s area, then find a square with that area.
problems.solution: The shared area is $18\times8=144\text{ cm}^{2}$. Since $12^{2}=144$, the square has side 12 cm and perimeter $4\times12=48\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle labelled 18 cm by 8 cm and a square with no side lengths. They have equal areas.

problems.q: Two squares have side lengths differing by 3 cm. Their combined perimeter is 68 cm. Find their combined area.
problems.hint: Divide the combined perimeter by four. This gives the sum of the two side lengths.
problems.solution: The side lengths add to $68\div4=17$ cm and differ by 3 cm. Removing the difference leaves $17-3=14$ cm for two equal smaller lengths, so the sides are 7 cm and 10 cm. The combined area is $7^{2}+10^{2}=149\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A smaller square and a larger square. Their side lengths differ by 3 cm and their combined perimeter is 68 cm. Neither side length is labelled.

problems.q: A rectangle measures 12 cm by 7 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Multiply the number of square centimetres in a row by the number of rows.
problems.solution: The rectangle has area $12\times7=84\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle with adjacent sides labelled 12 cm and 7 cm.

problems.q: A rectangle measures 15 cm by 4 cm. Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: There are two sides of each length.
problems.solution: The perimeter is $15+4+15+4=38\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle with adjacent sides labelled 15 cm and 4 cm.

problems.q: A rectangle has area 96 cm² and width 8 cm. Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: Use the area and width to find the length before adding the boundary lengths.
problems.solution: The length is $96\div8=12$ cm. The perimeter is $2\times(12+8)=40\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle labelled area 96 square centimetres, with width 8 cm. Its length is unknown.

problems.q: A rectangle has perimeter 70 cm and length 22 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Half the perimeter is the length plus the width.
problems.solution: The length and width add to $70\div2=35$ cm. The width is $35-22=13$ cm, so the area is $22\times13=286\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle labelled perimeter 70 cm and length 22 cm. Its width is unknown.

problems.q: An 18 cm by 12 cm rectangle is divided into 3 equal vertical strips. Find the perimeter of the shaded strip.
problems.hint: The strip keeps the full height, but has only a share of the total width.
problems.solution: Each strip is $18\div3=6$ cm wide and 12 cm high. Its perimeter is $2\times(6+12)=36\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: An 18 cm wide, 12 cm high rectangle divided into 3 equal vertical strips. The left strip is shaded. No strip width is labelled.

problems.q: Rectangles A and B measure 9 cm by 15 cm and 11 cm by 13 cm respectively. Both have perimeter 48 cm. Which has the larger area, and by how much?
problems.hint: Equal perimeters do not guarantee equal areas. Calculate the two products.
problems.solution: Area A is $9\times15=135\text{ cm}^{2}$. Area B is $11\times13=143\text{ cm}^{2}$. B has the larger area, by $143-135=8\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: Rectangle A has sides 9 cm and 15 cm; rectangle B has sides 11 cm and 13 cm. Neither area is shown.

problems.q: A 2 cm by 3 cm rectangle is removed from the top-right corner of an 11 cm by 7 cm rectangle. Find the perimeter of the remaining L-shaped figure.
problems.hint: Compare the outer edges that were removed with the new edges created by the cut.
problems.solution: The cut removes boundary lengths of 2 cm and 3 cm, then replaces them with new edges of the same lengths. The perimeter stays $2\times(11+7)=36\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: An L-shaped figure made from an 11 cm wide, 7 cm high rectangle by removing a top-right corner 2 cm wide and 3 cm high. Only these four given lengths are labelled.

problems.q: A rectangular frame has outer dimensions 16 cm by 12 cm. Its border is 2 cm wide on every side. Find the area of the shaded border.
problems.hint: There is a border at both ends of each inner dimension.
problems.solution: The inner dimensions are $16-2-2=12$ cm and $12-2-2=8$ cm. Subtract the opening from the outer rectangle: $16\times12-12\times8=192-96=96\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangular frame with outer dimensions 16 cm by 12 cm and a uniform 2 cm border. The border is shaded. The inner dimensions are unlabelled.

problems.q: A rectangle’s length is 3 times its width. Its perimeter is 64 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Think of the width as one part and the length as three parts.
problems.solution: Half the perimeter is $64\div2=32$ cm. This is 4 width-sized parts, so the width is $32\div4=8$ cm and the length is 24 cm. The area is $24\times8=192\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle labelled perimeter 64 cm. The width is marked w and the length 3w, with no numerical side lengths.

problems.q: A rectangle has area 144 cm² and perimeter 50 cm. Its side lengths are whole numbers of centimetres. Find its length and width.
problems.hint: Look for a factor pair of the area whose sum is half the perimeter.
problems.solution: The two side lengths multiply to 144 and add to $50\div2=25$. The factor pair 9 and 16 works: $9\times16=144$ and $9+16=25$. The rectangle is 16 cm by 9 cm.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangle with unknown length and width. Its area is 144 square centimetres and its perimeter is 50 cm. No numerical side lengths are shown.

problems.q: A parallelogram has base 11 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Use the distance measured at a right angle to the base.
problems.solution: The area is base times perpendicular height: $11\times6=66\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram with base 11 cm and a dashed perpendicular height labelled 6 cm. The height has a right-angle marker.

problems.q: A parallelogram has base 15 cm and sloping side 8 cm. Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: Opposite sides of a parallelogram have equal lengths.
problems.solution: There are two sides of each length, so the perimeter is $2\times(15+8)=46\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram with base 15 cm and a sloping side labelled 8 cm. No height is marked.

problems.q: A parallelogram has base 13 cm, sloping side 9 cm, and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Which measurement meets the base at a right angle?
problems.solution: The perpendicular height is 7 cm. The 9 cm sloping side is unnecessary for area. Use $13\times7=91\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram with base 13 cm, sloping side 9 cm and dashed perpendicular height 7 cm. A right-angle marker identifies the height.

problems.q: A parallelogram has area 108 cm² and base 18 cm. Find its perpendicular height.
problems.hint: Undo multiplication by the base.
problems.solution: Since area equals base times height, the height is $108\div18=6\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram labelled area 108 square centimetres and base 18 cm. Its dashed perpendicular height is labelled h.

problems.q: A parallelogram has perimeter 58 cm and one side 19 cm long. Find the length of an adjacent side.
problems.hint: Half the perimeter contains one side of each length.
problems.solution: The adjacent side is $58\div2-19=29-19=10\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram labelled perimeter 58 cm. One side is 19 cm and the adjacent side is marked with a question mark.

problems.q: Two parallelograms lean at different angles. Each has base 12 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. What is the difference between their areas?
problems.hint: Decide which measurements determine each area.
problems.solution: Each area is $12\times5=60\text{ cm}^{2}$. Changing the lean while keeping the base and height fixed leaves the area unchanged, so the difference is $0\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: Two parallelograms with different slopes. Both have base 12 cm and dashed perpendicular height 5 cm. Neither area is shown.

problems.q: A parallelogram has base 16 cm and height 9 cm. A diagonal divides it into two triangles. Find the area of the shaded triangle.
problems.hint: The shaded triangle has the same base and perpendicular height as the parallelogram.
problems.solution: The triangle has area $\frac{1}{2}\times16\times9=72\text{ cm}^{2}$. Equivalently, a diagonal divides the parallelogram into two equal-area triangles.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram with base 16 cm and perpendicular height 9 cm. A diagonal joins opposite corners and one of the two triangles is shaded.

problems.q: A parallelogram has the same area as a 9 cm by 14 cm rectangle. Its base is 18 cm. Find its perpendicular height.
problems.hint: Find the shared area using the rectangle, then work backward with the parallelogram.
problems.solution: The shared area is $9\times14=126\text{ cm}^{2}$. The parallelogram’s height is $126\div18=7\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A 9 cm by 14 cm rectangle and an equal-area parallelogram. The parallelogram has base 18 cm and an unknown perpendicular height h.

problems.q: A parallelogram has perimeter 50 cm, sloping side 11 cm, and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Use the perimeter to find the base, then pair that base with its perpendicular height.
problems.solution: The base is $50\div2-11=14$ cm. The area is $14\times7=98\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram labelled perimeter 50 cm, with a sloping side of 11 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Its base is labelled b.

problems.q: A parallelogram has area 120 cm² and perpendicular height 8 cm. Its base is 3 cm longer than its sloping side. Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: Recover the base from the area, then use the difference between the two side lengths.
problems.solution: The base is $120\div8=15$ cm, so the sloping side is $15-3=12$ cm. The perimeter is $2\times(15+12)=54\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A parallelogram labelled area 120 square centimetres and perpendicular height 8 cm. Its base and sloping side are unknown; the base is 3 cm longer.

problems.q: A triangle has base 14 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: A triangle occupies half the area of a parallelogram with the same base and height.
problems.solution: The area is $\frac{1}{2}\times14\times8=56\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A triangle with base 14 cm and dashed perpendicular height 8 cm, marked with a right angle.

problems.q: A triangle has sides 9 cm, 10 cm, and 13 cm. Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: Add the lengths around the triangle.
problems.solution: The perimeter is $9+10+13=32\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A triangle with sides labelled 9 cm, 10 cm and 13 cm.

problems.q: A triangle has area 45 cm² and base 15 cm. Find its perpendicular height.
problems.hint: Double the area before dividing by the base.
problems.solution: Because $A=\frac{1}{2} bh$, the height is $2\times45\div15=6\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A triangle labelled area 45 square centimetres and base 15 cm. Its dashed perpendicular height is labelled h.

problems.q: A right triangle has perpendicular sides measuring 12 cm and 7 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: The two sides meeting at the right angle can serve as the base and height.
problems.solution: The perpendicular sides give $\frac{1}{2}\times12\times7=42\text{ cm}^{2}$. The third side is unnecessary.
problems.imageAlt: A rotated right triangle with perpendicular sides labelled 12 cm and 7 cm. The right angle is marked; the third side is unlabelled.

problems.q: An obtuse triangle has base 16 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. The height is drawn outside the triangle. Find its area.
problems.hint: A perpendicular height may meet an extension of the base.
problems.solution: The outside segment still measures the perpendicular height. Use $\frac{1}{2}\times16\times5=40\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: An obtuse triangle with base 16 cm. A dashed height of 5 cm meets the extension of the base outside the triangle, with a right-angle marker at its foot.

problems.q: An isosceles triangle has perimeter 38 cm and base 12 cm. Find the length of each equal side.
problems.hint: Remove the base length from the perimeter, then share the remainder equally.
problems.solution: The equal sides together measure $38-12=26$ cm. Each is $26\div2=13\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: An isosceles triangle labelled perimeter 38 cm and base 12 cm. Matching ticks mark its two equal sides; their lengths are unlabelled.

problems.q: A diagonal divides an 18 cm by 10 cm rectangle into two triangles. Find the area of the shaded triangle.
problems.hint: The diagonal divides the rectangle into two equal-area triangles.
problems.solution: The rectangle has area $18\times10=180\text{ cm}^{2}$. Half of it is $180\div2=90\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: An 18 cm by 10 cm rectangle split by a diagonal, with one triangle shaded. No diagonal length is given.

problems.q: Two triangles each have base 12 cm. Their perpendicular heights are 7 cm and 11 cm. Find the difference between their areas.
problems.hint: Compute the two areas, or use the difference between their heights.
problems.solution: The areas are $\frac{1}{2}\times12\times7=42\text{ cm}^{2}$ and $\frac{1}{2}\times12\times11=66\text{ cm}^{2}$. Their difference is $66-42=24\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: Two triangles, both with base 12 cm. Their dashed perpendicular heights are labelled 7 cm and 11 cm. No areas are shown.

problems.q: A triangle has base 24 cm and height 10 cm. A line parallel to the base cuts off a smaller triangle at the top, with base 12 cm and height 5 cm. Find the shaded area below that line.
problems.hint: Subtract the smaller triangle’s area from the whole triangle’s area.
problems.solution: The whole triangle has area $\frac{1}{2}\times24\times10=120\text{ cm}^{2}$. The small triangle has area $\frac{1}{2}\times12\times5=30\text{ cm}^{2}$. The shaded area is $120-30=90\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A triangle with base 24 cm and perpendicular height 10 cm. A parallel segment of length 12 cm cuts off a top triangle of height 5 cm. The region below the segment is shaded.

problems.q: A triangle has area 120 cm². Two segments from the top vertex divide its base in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5, forming three triangles. Find the area of the shaded middle triangle.
problems.hint: The three smaller triangles share the same perpendicular height. Compare their bases.
problems.solution: With a common height, the three areas are in the base ratio $2:3:5$. The middle triangle takes $\frac{3}{2+3+5}=\frac{3}{10}$ of the total area, so its area is $120\times\frac{3}{10}=36\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A triangle of total area 120 square centimetres, divided from its top vertex into three triangles. Base segments are labelled 2 parts, 3 parts and 5 parts from left to right. The middle triangle is shaded.

problems.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides 10 cm and 16 cm, and perpendicular height 5 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Use the average length of the two parallel sides with the height.
problems.solution: The area is $\frac{1}{2}\times(10+16)\times5=65\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A trapezoid with parallel sides 10 cm and 16 cm and dashed perpendicular height 5 cm. The parallel sides and right angle are marked.

problems.q: An isosceles trapezoid has parallel sides 8 cm and 14 cm, and equal sloping sides 5 cm long. Find its perimeter.
problems.hint: Add all four boundary sides, including both equal sloping sides.
problems.solution: The perimeter is $8+14+5+5=32\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: An isosceles trapezoid with parallel sides 8 cm and 14 cm. One sloping side is labelled 5 cm and both legs carry matching equal-length ticks. No height is shown.

problems.q: A trapezoid has parallel bases 8 cm and 14 cm and height 6 cm. A diagonal divides it into two triangles. Find the area of the larger triangle.
problems.hint: Each triangle can use one parallel side as its base. Compare the corresponding heights.
problems.solution: Both triangles have height 6 cm, so the one with base 14 cm is larger. Its area is $\frac{1}{2}\times14\times6=42\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A trapezoid with parallel bases 8 cm and 14 cm, perpendicular height 6 cm, and one diagonal. Neither of the resulting triangles is highlighted.

problems.q: A trapezoid has area 88 cm² and parallel sides 8 cm and 14 cm. Find its perpendicular height.
problems.hint: Find the average of the parallel side lengths, then divide the area by that average.
problems.solution: The average base length is $(8+14)\div2=11$ cm. The height is $88\div11=8\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A trapezoid labelled area 88 square centimetres, with parallel sides 8 cm and 14 cm. Its dashed perpendicular height is labelled h.

problems.q: A trapezoid has area 90 cm², perpendicular height 6 cm, and one parallel side 12 cm. Find the other parallel side.
problems.hint: Use twice the area divided by the height to find the sum of the parallel sides.
problems.solution: The parallel sides add to $2\times90\div6=30$ cm. The unknown side is $30-12=18\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A trapezoid labelled area 90 square centimetres, with one parallel side 12 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. The other parallel side is marked with a question mark.

problems.q: A trapezoid has vertical parallel sides measuring 7 cm and 13 cm. The horizontal distance between them is 8 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: A base can be vertical. Use the distance measured perpendicular to the parallel sides.
problems.solution: The parallel sides are 7 cm and 13 cm, with perpendicular distance 8 cm. The area is $\frac{1}{2}\times(7+13)\times8=80\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A sideways trapezoid whose vertical parallel sides are 7 cm and 13 cm. A horizontal dashed segment between them is labelled 8 cm and meets a side at a right angle.

problems.q: An isosceles trapezoid has bases 8 cm and 20 cm, perpendicular height 8 cm, and sloping sides 10 cm long. Find its area.
problems.hint: Choose the perpendicular height rather than a sloping side.
problems.solution: Use the 8 cm height with the two parallel bases: $\frac{1}{2}\times(8+20)\times8=112\text{ cm}^{2}$. The 10 cm legs are unnecessary for this calculation.
problems.imageAlt: An isosceles trapezoid with bases 8 cm and 20 cm, equal legs labelled 10 cm, and a dashed perpendicular height of 8 cm. Matching ticks identify the equal legs.

problems.q: A trapezoid has bases 12 cm and 20 cm and height 6 cm. Perpendiculars from the shorter base divide it into a central rectangle and two shaded triangles. Find their combined shaded area.
problems.hint: Subtract the central rectangle from the whole trapezoid, or combine the two triangle bases.
problems.solution: The trapezoid has area $\frac{1}{2}\times(12+20)\times6=96\text{ cm}^{2}$. The central rectangle has area $12\times6=72\text{ cm}^{2}$. The shaded triangles total $96-72=24\text{ cm}^{2}$.
problems.imageAlt: A trapezoid with bases 12 cm and 20 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Two perpendicular segments form a central rectangle. The two outside corner triangles are shaded; their individual base lengths are unlabelled.

problems.q: A trapezoid has the same area as a 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle. Its height is 8 cm and its shorter base is 9 cm. Find its longer base.
problems.hint: Find the shared area, then work backward through the trapezoid area formula.
problems.solution: The shared area is $12\times8=96\text{ cm}^{2}$. The trapezoid’s bases add to $2\times96\div8=24$ cm. Its longer base is $24-9=15\text{ cm}$.
problems.imageAlt: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle and an equal-area trapezoid. The trapezoid has shorter base 9 cm and height 8 cm; its longer base is labelled b.

problems.q: An isosceles trapezoid has perimeter 60 cm. Its shorter base is 12 cm, its equal sloping sides are each 13 cm, and its height is 12 cm. Find its area.
problems.hint: Recover the missing base from the perimeter before using the perpendicular height.
problems.solution: The longer base is $60-12-13-13=22$ cm. The area is $\frac{1}{2}\times(12+22)\times12=204\text{ cm}^{2}$. The 13 cm legs are used for perimeter, while the 12 cm height is used for area.
problems.imageAlt: An isosceles trapezoid labelled perimeter 60 cm. Its shorter base is 12 cm, its matching legs are 13 cm, and its perpendicular height is 12 cm. The longer base is labelled b.
